research_mode: official UK government and ONS primary statistical publications and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Youth-justice scope
verified_claims: The annual publication covers children aged 10 to 17 in the England and Wales youth justice system.
limitations: Some sections include different reference periods and must not be combined without labels.

sources.name: Multiple-source compilation
verified_claims: The publication combines data from the Home Office, Ministry of Justice, youth justice services and Youth Custody Service.
limitations: The sources use different systems and quality processes.

sources.name: Annual reference period
verified_claims: Most statistics cover 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025 where available.
limitations: Some first-time-entrant and criminal-history data use the year ending December 2024.

sources.name: Rounding convention
verified_claims: Large figures are rounded to the nearest hundred and smaller figures to the nearest ten in commentary.
limitations: Percentages are calculated from unrounded data, so displayed totals may not reproduce exactly.

sources.name: Unknown-ethnicity treatment
verified_claims: Unknown ethnicity is included for arrests and sentencing occasions because of its increased volume.
limitations: Unknown values must not be assigned to another ethnicity group.

sources.name: Child stop-and-search count
verified_claims: There were about 95,900 stop and searches of children in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: A stop-and-search count is not a count of unique children.

sources.name: Child stop-and-search change
verified_claims: Child stop and searches decreased by 7% from the previous year.
limitations: Changes can reflect police activity and recording as well as underlying behaviour.

sources.name: No-further-action share
verified_claims: About 74% of child stop and searches resulted in no further action.
limitations: No further action is not proof that the search lacked lawful grounds.

sources.name: Arrest outcome share
verified_claims: About 10% of child stop and searches resulted in arrest.
limitations: The proportion is not an individual probability and varies by context.

sources.name: Child arrest count
verified_claims: There were about 58,300 arrests of children for notifiable offences.
limitations: Arrest counts are not unique-offender or conviction counts.

sources.name: Long-term arrest change
verified_claims: Child arrests were 38% lower than in the year ending March 2015.
limitations: Long-term changes can reflect policy, demographics and recording changes.

sources.name: First-time-entrant count
verified_claims: There were just over 8,100 child first-time entrants in the year ending December 2024.
limitations: First-time entrant means first recorded caution or sentence, not first harmful act.

sources.name: First-time-entrant period boundary
verified_claims: March 2025 first-time-entrant data were unavailable, so the publication uses December 2024.
limitations: The FTE period must not be presented as matching the March-year sections.

sources.name: Proven-offence count
verified_claims: Children committed about 35,600 proven offences in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: Proven offences are justice outcomes and exclude unreported or unproven incidents.

sources.name: Offence-group revision
verified_claims: Youth Justice Board revised offence groups for the latest publication.
limitations: Most offence-group changes cannot be compared directly with earlier years.

sources.name: Reoffending cohort size
verified_claims: The child reoffending cohort was about 14,500 for the year ending March 2024.
limitations: The cohort uses an earlier period because reoffending requires follow-up time.

sources.name: Child reoffender count
verified_claims: About 4,600 children in the cohort reoffended.
limitations: The count depends on the proven-reoffending definition and waiting period.

sources.name: Child reoffence count
verified_claims: The cohort generated about 20,500 proven reoffences.
limitations: Reoffence counts are not a measure of current parcel danger.

sources.name: Adult-comparison boundary
verified_claims: The bulletin compares youth and adult system measures in a dedicated chapter.
limitations: Differences in age, offence mix and disposals prevent simple effectiveness rankings.

sources.name: Local-level data boundary
verified_claims: The release provides local-level tables and maps.
limitations: Local administrative areas do not establish exact incident addresses or parcel-level outcomes.
